entries.title: Relocation
entries.text:
Ladies and Gents, due to a 'change in management' thanks to the fine folks in the central chamber, Dr. Ken's Chem Den is relocating to Mosstown! If any part of that pink lump in your cranium still works, I'd suggest you do the same. 

I look forward to continuing your treatment with the same high-quality chems at the same low prices!

entries.title: Business Hours
entries.text:
I'm here Tuesdays and Thursdays from whenever the hell I wake up to right before sundown when the creepy crawlies come out. 

Remember the slogan - "Feeding your addiction with the highest quality chems you can afford!"

entries.title: Menu
entries.text:
Standard Fare: Glue and paints for your sniffing needs! Buffout and booze for those seeking a good time on a budget.

The Hard Stuff: Med-X, Psycho. Locked behind the counter so you're gonna have to ask for it. You think I'd keep it on the shelf for you junkies to steal?

Exotic Tastes: Hear me out. If you're looking for the cutting edge of getting high, some of my more adventurous customers told me they got a real rush inhaling the fumes of... well, cow droppings. So if that's your thing, let me know.

Boring Doctor Things: I guess if you have a cold or snot ear or something I can dig up a disease cure. But it'll cost you!

items.name: For Maude
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Hello, 'Maudy'. Hopefully you're still alive to hear this after my... modifications to the bot targeting parameters.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: If you are, you have probably noticed that all the exits topside are sealed shut and you are... *laughs*... so screwed!

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: I get it, Maude. You thought you were safe. You thought you built a home for all those helpless saps down here and refused to give way to how the world really works now.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Yeah... That's how I knew you'd pull some dumb shit like this.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Before you and your crew ran off into the tunnels like a bunch of rats, you asked me why I was doing all of this.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Now, the reasoning is... it's pretty simple: the mean guys always win, Maude.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Things are no different now than before the bombs. Hell, it's the reason most of us landed down here in the first place!

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: I just figured I may as well be the one to mean up before somebody else beat me to it.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: *Laughs* Sorry, I was just thinking how my daddy would be so proud of me. You know, that his boy followed in his footsteps in 'waste management'. I will see you in hell, Maude.

items.name: Marcus' Speech
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Alright people, settle in, settle in. Alright. Now, I asked that all the Burrows folk gather here today because I'm making a little announcement.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: As of right now, the Burrows Boys are withdrawing from our little alliance and claiming ownership over these tunnels.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Now... for some of you that is probably confusing. Maybe you're asking yourself "Marcus, what's that mean for the Burrows? What's it mean for me?"

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Well friends, it's really pretty damn simple. It means that as of now, I own everything in these tunnels!

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: The rats you eat, the mold growing on your mattress, the bricks you are standing on. They're all mine.
*Crowd Murmuring*

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: But, not to worry. I will be a kind and fair ruler. I will let you continue using my facilities if you obey one very simple rule.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: And that is to follow my every order to a T! I tell you to do something, you do it. I need something, you get it.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: I ask you for the moon? You figure out how to pull that SOB out of the sky and bring it right down here to me.

transcript.speaker: Trish
transcript.text: And if we refuse?

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Well you could do that... you could. But you'd be more screwed than you already are. Look around, Trish.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: My boys are the only ones here with guns, and the only ones that know anything about fighting! None of you can touch us. You wouldn't stand a chance.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: I understand you folks have gotten used to the chummy, love-your-neighbor bullshit, but the new world order is here.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Now, I get it. That is some bitter medicine to swallow. But if I need to help you force it down, just know that I am more than happy to oblige.

entries.title: Work Log: Last Day
entries.text:

I understand the systems will find and fix errors quicker but what I don't understand is where the hell they get off ruining a man's livelihood.

I added an executable to the turret defense system they're so proud of. Just a little parting gift before they kick me out. It would be a real shame if something - or someone - 'accidentally' activated them...

entries.title: Initial Tests

entries.text:
The Raiders chased us for almost two hours before my daughter Darlene spotted the treehouse. We scrambled up the rope ladder, praying they wouldn't follow. We crouched low and waited until the Raiders passed beneath. That's when we opened fire. 

Our elevated position gave us a huge advantage, and we took them down in seconds. I don't think they even knew where the shots were coming from. It was at that moment we knew that our Free States group had found a new home.

While the thought of living in a makeshift tree fort seemed clever, we didn't realize the huge amount of work we'd have ahead of us. 

Caroline volunteered to hike down to Gavin Mccullough's cabin to see if his group wanted to join up. Before the war, Gavin was a master carpenter, so he'd have the skills and tools to get the job done. 

Fortunately for us, his group agreed to give us a hand. With their help, and Gavin's know-how, we had a solid platform built within a day. We were exhausted, but Gavin promised that the best was yet to come.

It's been a little over a month and our dream of a tree fort has turned into more of a treehouse village. 

Gavin designed a way to use other nearby trees to build a series of interconnected platforms. It was pretty damn clever - everyone would have their own platform with living quarters and a roof over their heads. We would be close to each other, but each group would still have some privacy. 

Finding that child's treehouse was turning out to be the luckiest thing that ever happened to us.

I woke to gunshots and Gavin yelling that we were under attack by Raiders. We ran to the windows and returned fire. 

We were able to run the Raiders off, but the damage was done. We had lost Darlene. It was clear that our treehouse village wasn't enough to keep everyone safe. The Raiders would keep coming, and then slowly, we'd keep dying.

We decided to give up our home and move on, to look for somewhere safer. I'm going to leave a few traps behind as a parting gift, just in case the Raiders return to finish the job. A little payback for what they did to my sweet Darlene.

FROM THE PASTOR'S DESK:

Greetings, and Welcome to Vault 94!

On behalf of the Vault 94 intentional community, it is my pleasure to welcome you to our home. Vault 94 is founded on the principles of faith, nonviolence, and communal life in harmony with nature. Whether you share our beliefs or choose to walk your own path, know that you are always welcome among us.

Vault 94 was blessed with an abundance of resources, and we are committed to sharing them with all in need as we work together to restore the bounty of the Earth. More importantly, we hope to share our values and rebuild a common belief in the essential goodness of humanity.

If you are hungry, come and eat. If you are weary, come and rest. If you are here to trade, our stores are always open. Welcome to Vault 94. Welcome home.

--Pastor Gabriella Salavar

P.S. Please check any weapons or explosives at the reception desk as you enter.

entries.title: Vault 94 Overview

VAULT 94 OVERVIEW

Welcome to Vault 94!

Thank you for accepting our invitation to be a part of the Vault-Tec Societal Preservation Program. Vault 94 has been developed to respect the values and beliefs of your intentional community, as outlined in the documents submitted with your application.

- FAITH. With the exception of one (1) Vault-Tec Maintenance Engineer, all invited residents of this Vault are members of your congregation.
- NONVIOLENCE. No weapons or ammunition has been provided, nor have any turrets or other defensive systems been installed. All robots have been locked to a nonviolent conflict resolution mode.
- COMMUNAL LIFE. Living Quarters have been clustered to create communal residential spaces instead of individual residences. A Community Council model of government (see COMMUNITY GOVERNANCE) will encourage dialogue and consensus-building among residents.
- ECOLOGICAL HARMONY. Vault 94 houses extensive agricultural facilities. You are encouraged to use these for the benefit of your community and any other survivors of a nuclear apocalypse (see MISSION & FACILITIES).

entries.title: Vault 94 Community Governance
entries.text:
VAULT 94 COMMUNITY GOVERNANCE

In keeping with your community's values and beliefs, Vault 94 has not been assigned an Overseer. Instead, your Vault is to be governed by a Community Council composed of the residents. All Vault Residents are encouraged to attend and participate in Community Council sessions.

A terminal in the Community Council Chamber will automatically record the minutes and motions before the Council. The Council is encouraged to operate by consensus, and consensus will be presumed unless otherwise indicated. Motions related to Vault Security will require a formal vote, which. in accord with the Vault 94 Community Governance Charter requires a vote of all registered Vault Residents.

entries.title: Vault 94 Mission & Facilities
entries.text:
VAULT 94 MISSION & FACILITIES

In the event of global nuclear war, multiple mass extinction events are anticipated. The primary mission of Vault 94 is to monitor and stabilize the local ecosystem, and to assist survivors outside the Vault (if any) with their agricultural needs.

To that end, Vault 94 has been equipped with a complete agricultural research facility, including experimental greenhouses, aquaculture labs, and a comprehensive seed bank containing all known plants suitable for edible or medicinal use.

To prevent damage to the seed bank, your Vault Door will automatically seal when external radiation reaches unsafe levels. The Vault Door may be reopened at your discretion after a mandatory minimum shelter period of one year. Vault Residents are encouraged to work with other survivors (if any) to assess the state of the environment and work to improve it.

Vault 94 has also been selected to receive a Garden of Eden Creation Kit (G.E.C.K.) module. In the event of catastrophic environmental devastation, your G.E.C.K. may be the best hope for the survival of humanity. As a security precaution, and to prevent premature use or misuse, the G.E.C.K. has been sealed in a self-contained secure wing of the Vault. Access to the G.E.C.K. Wing requires special authorization from the Vault 94 Community Council.

The Vault 94 Vault Door has been linked to the Vault's external radiation sensors. The door will automatically close once radiation outside the Vault reaches levels consistent with a significant nuclear event. entries.title: Overview
entries.text:
VAULT-TEC EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM: AN OVERVIEW

Congratulations! Your Vault has been equipped with the latest automated emergency response technology: the Vault-Tec Emergency Management System.

The Emergency Management System is a comprehensive database of automated contingency protocols developed to assist Overseers, Vault Residents, and (when/if available) Certified Vault-Tec Emergency Responders in identifying, diagnosing, and resolving a wide array of potential emergency situations.

entries.menu: Emergency Management System › Emergency Management System Documentation
entries.title: Using the Emergency Management System
entries.text:
USING THE EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM:

In the unlikely event of an emergency, your Vault Mainframe will automatically assess the situation and select an appropriate error resolution protocol from the Emergency Management System database. Populated by thousands of programs submitted by Vault-Tec University's talented undergraduate students, your database holds the solution to any problem.

When applicable, your Vault may broadcast an emergency transmission to any Vault-Tec personnel in the area. Response times in the aftermath of a nuclear conflict may vary.

The emergency response team leader should use any available terminal to activate the Emergency Management System and indicate their team's level of expertise. This will calibrate the protocol and adjust applicable hazard pay or bonuses, if any.

Thereafter, simply follow the audible instructions from the Vault Mainframe. The Mainframe will continually monitor the situation and introduce additional contingencies as required.

entries.menu: Emergency Management System › Emergency Management System Documentation
entries.title: Example Protocol: Catastrophic Flooding
entries.text:
VAULT-TEC EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM:
ERROR CODE: [FC-855] Catastrophic Flooding

SUMMARY PROTOCOL:
- Locate, Seal or Repair Rupture.
- Protocol Method Unavailable... 
- Activate Emergency Flood Control Procedure K-52.

STUDENT DEVELOPER: Yeates, Kylee (VP205, 2074)
DEVELOPER NOTES:
- This protocol identifies the safest route through the Vault, assesses the flooding in each successive section along this route, and directs repairs as needed to drain them and allow the team to proceed.
- Secondary protocols address contingencies including pump, reactor, and structural failure, ventilation issues, and resident evacuation.

PROFESSOR: DeMarcos, E.
GRADE: B+
REMARKS: A competent protocol that appropriately handles most major contingencies. Notable flaws include an overly cautious pathing algorithm (simulations suggest unnecessarily circuitous route selection), a tendency to overstress Flood Control Pumps with excessive drainage, and an inability to reset the pumps automatically.

entries.menu: Emergency Management System › Emergency Management System Documentation
entries.title: Example Protocol: Nuclear Incident
entries.text:
VAULT-TEC EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM:
ERROR CODE: [RZ-504] Nuclear Incident

SUMMARY PROTOCOL:
- Proceed to the Operations Center.
- Identify the source of the radiation.
- Neutralize the threat.

STUDENT DEVELOPER: Michaels, Ted (VP101, 2076)
DEVELOPER NOTES:
- This protocol relies on the Vault's internal sensors to sample radioactive isotopes at multiple points, then applies a gradient heuristic to identify the source of the radiation and propose a resolution.
- Supported radiation sources include nuclear detonation (external or internal), fusion core cascade failures, reactors, and a G.E.C.K.

PROFESSOR: DeMarcos, E.
GRADE: C
REMARKS: Adequate but uninspired work for a 100-level course. While generally successful at basic containment, this protocol fails to address potential secondary contingencies and may leave the emergency response team without sufficient guidance to address them. In particular, its inability to override security seals of Class-III or above may prove problematic if the source of the radiation is in a secure area. Still, no worse than all the other student submissions for this error code.

entries.menu: Emergency Management System › Emergency Management System Documentation
entries.title: Example Protocol: Containment Breach
entries.text:
VAULT-TEC EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM:
ERROR CODE: [AX-481]  Containment Breach

SUMMARY PROTOCOL:
- Protocol Method Unavailable... 
- Activate Emergency Flooding Procedure M-09.
- Evacuate the Vault.

STUDENT DEVELOPER: Lanning, Jim (VP205, 2077)
DEVELOPER NOTES: -NONE-

PROFESSOR: DeMarcos, E.
GRADE: F
REMARKS: This program does not crash immediately. 

Regrettably, that is its only positive characteristic. While completely flooding a Vault would doubtless be effective at dealing with containment breach of the vault seals (or virtually anything else), the extreme and potentially irreversible nature of this solution should have made it a last resort. Instead, this protocol opts for it immediately. It then fails to provide sufficient time for Vault Residents to evacuate, fails to safely shut down Vault Systems or override safeguards that could impede the evacuation, and fails to verify that bulkhead doors located along the evacuation route are even open. An evacuation might be successful if the Residents aggressively damage the flood control system to delay the procedure, but Vault-Tec does not typically encourage Residents to destroy their Vault. 

Unfortunately, this is the only extant submission for this particular error code. Recommend soliciting a replacement from this Fall's class.

OVERSEER EYES ONLY | VIOLATION VTP-01011

You have been selected as the special Overseer for Vault 94.

Vault 94 is designed to test the adaptability of ideological groups to changing social contexts. The selected residents are all members of an agrarian pacifist religious community, and are expected to reinforce that identity during the one-year shelter period. Thereafter, they have been encouraged to open the Vault to other survivors, who will likely be armed and desperate. Vault 94 has been allocated high-value resources, but no weapons or other defenses. The residents will need to modify their belief system, improvise, and adapt quickly in order to ensure their survival.

In order to minimize disruptions to their social order and avoid contaminating the experiment, you will be the sole representative of Vault-Tec in this Vault. You are to maintain your current assignment as a Vault-Tec Maintenance Engineer and minimize your interaction with the other residents. The Vault will be self-governing; you have no authority and are to avoid any role in their decision-making process.

Once the initial shelter period ends, you are to encourage the residents to reopen the Vault if they have not already done so. Observe the ensuing conflicts and report your findings using the secure channel provided.

entries.title: Personal Log - 10/24/77
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 10-24-77
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

I can't sleep. Can't shake the sound of them, pounding outside the Vault Door.

I went for a walk around 2am. Found the Pastor's daughter crying out in the Atrium. We talked for a while. She seems like a nice girl. She deserved better than this. We all did.

What the hell, Vault-Tec? I'm an engineer, not a secret agent. I mean, sure, grateful not to be dead and all, but I never signed on for this. I wish I'd never enrolled at VTU.

entries.title: Personal Log - 11/2/77
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 11-2-77
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

It's strange, being an outsider in a community like this. Everyone knows everyone else; they all just get along. They don't curse, don't argue, barely even raise their voices. Everyone's still in shock, but there hasn't been a single fight. It would be creepy, if it wasn't so nice.

Pastor Salavar is still pretty cold. She blames me for all the people who got locked out, even if she won't say so. But everyone else is polite, even if they keep their distance.

entries.title: Personal Log - 1/14/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 1-14-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

I've been spending more time with Angelique. She's working as an aide in the Nursery, and I've always liked kids. We get along pretty well. Her mother keeps hovering, though, or sending people to check up on us. She still doesn't trust me.

entries.title: Personal Log - 3/6/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 3-6-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

Another Sunday, another Community Council meeting. I was reluctant to go at first-- it is against the Instructions-- but they need the technical expertise, and refusing would just seem suspicious. So long as I don't speak up too much, I'm sure it'll be all right.

entries.title: Personal Log - 5/29/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 5-29-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

I was always pretty solitary growing up. Living in a community like this, it's been different. Wish I'd had friends like this years ago.
 
I've started going to morning services. I don't know that I believe it all, but it seems to work for them. Might as well go along.

entries.title: Personal Log - 8/28/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 8-28-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

Angelique and I are engaged. We announced it at the Council meeting this afternoon. Pastor Salavar didn't take it well, but everyone else was happy for us. Angelique says I should just give her time. She'll come around.

entries.title: Personal Log - 10/5/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 10-5-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

The shelter period ends in a couple of weeks. The Council's been debating Salavar's Ambassador Program, to send people out in search of survivors and invite them to the Vault. I've done everything I can to talk them out of it, but they won't listen. Whatever's out there, they aren't ready for it. The world's not going to be the same.

Vault-Tec expects them to crack, ditch their beliefs, fight to survive. But I know these people. I'm one of them now. They won't do it. And I don't want them to.

entries.title: Personal Log - 10/16/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 10-16-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

I came clean. I told the Council everything, but they wouldn't believe me. So I showed them the damn Instructions.

Salavar was smug; said she was right about me all along. And Angelique... I've never seen her look at me like that before. It was horrible.

The Ambassador program passed anyway.

entries.title: Personal Log - 11/18/78
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG
Date: 11-18-78
User: Tyrone Hayes, Maintenance Engineer

The first Ambassadors are due back in a couple of days. Even now, we could seal the Vault and live here, safely, forever. Nothing has to change.

But they're convinced I'm wrong, that Vault-Tec was wrong. That whoever is left out there will finally understand the futility of war, that they'll be ready to listen, to live in peace.

I guess we'll see.

entries.text:
FROM THE PASTOR'S DESK:

Greetings, and Welcome to Vault 94!

On behalf of the Vault 94 intentional community, it is my pleasure to welcome you to our home. Vault 94 is founded on the principles of faith, nonviolence, and communal life in harmony with nature. Whether you share our beliefs or choose to walk your own path, know that you are always welcome among us.

Vault 94 was blessed with an abundance of resources, and we are committed to sharing them with all in need as we work together to restore the bounty of the Earth. More importantly, we hope to share our values and rebuild a common belief in the essential goodness of humanity.

If you are hungry, come and eat. If you are weary, come and rest. If you are here to trade, our stores are always open. Welcome to Vault 94. Welcome home.

--Pastor Gabriella Salavar

P.S. Please check any weapons or explosives at the reception desk as you enter.

transcript.text: A week ago, I was begging for food and was almost shot by someone who didn't want me near them. Well, I've had enough.

transcript.speaker: Unidentified Ghoul
transcript.text: I found a note from someone named Lucy Harwick. She claims to run a place where people like me can go to live their life without being afraid.

transcript.speaker: Unidentified Ghoul
transcript.text: I'm going to head out to Valley Galleria to see if it's true. I hope to god that it is, because I don't know how much more of this I can take.

items.name: About the Brotherhood
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: Thank you, Captain. It's just us.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Lizzy. What's on your mind?

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: A Brotherhood of Steel? What's that even mean? The men over here are confused.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: We need to do something bold.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: We can't just stay the US Army.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: What's going to happen, and this is only a matter of time, is some general, or some goddamned politician is going to exit a Vault and start ordering us around.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: And worse they'll order some grunt to start the whole damned cycle again.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Another wave of nuclear death. And if that's not enough they'll do it again.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: You know they will, Lizzy. It ends with us. We won't let them.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: I... I understand. But a Brotherhood? Knights? I'm supposed to call you, what, Elder?

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Words have power, Lizzy. They build identity. They take on a meaning if you keep using them, even if it didn't exist to begin with.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: It was the Knights and Scribes after the fall of Rome that protected what was left of Western civilization.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: So we are the new Knights and our role is similar.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: But we'll need more than names. We'll need new traditions, our own, well, mythology.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Something people can believe to their core.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: Is this necessary?

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: What else can I do? Declare myself President? Make you a Senator?

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Look around. Something's killing us more than the rads and freaks out there.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Depression. People have lost everyone. Every goddam soul. Wives, kids, loved ones, heck even the mailman.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: We need to replace it with something otherwise people's souls will wither. We'll be little more than walking dead men.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: I'll do my best to see the orders carried out, sir.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Give it time, Lizzy. People have a hunger to believe in something. Just let them work their way to it.

items.name: Captain's Log #1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: Ever since I washed up on these shores, my mind's felt more and more adrift. I'm hopin' this might be a way to keep me anchored.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: My name is Captain Raymond Clark. My father was a bosun and so was his father before him.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: My mother's name was Deidre and she had long, flaxen hair. Ah, this is foolish. How do I stop this thing? *grumble*

items.name: Captain's Log #2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: It's been a few weeks, or months, since I recorded one of these. Whole seasons seem to go by without my noticing.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: My head's been so clouded, I can barely keep track of what state we're in. Come on Raymond, hold it together.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: My name is Captain Raymond Clark. My father was a bosun. My mother's name was... was... Ah confound it!

items.name: Captain's Log #3
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Captain Raymond Clark
transcript.text: My name is Captain... Captain... I'm a Captain. It's my job to, to fish? To catch as many fish as we can. My father was a fish, and my mother...

items.name: Dear Riley
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: Hey Riley, it's mom! Just wanted to send you this holotape you can play in case you miss us.

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: We're so proud of you going on your first big adventure! You're going to have so much fun with all your friends!

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: I want you to be sure to listen to everything the scout masters and rangers tell you.

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: Remember, most of them are real people, so you can't throw things at them them like your Ms. Nanny.

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: So I don't want to hear any bad reports or get any phone calls in the middle of the night.

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: Mommy and daddy are on vacation, too, okay?

transcript.speaker: Becca
transcript.text: We love you very much, and miss you every day! And remember... Best behavior!

items.name: Ella's Log: Harpers Ferry
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: May 2, 2080. Jesus I'm tired. Ever since we agreed to help rebuild Harpers, it's just been non-stop work.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: These people are in some bad shape. Some are improving, but it pains me to see our supplies dwindle.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: It's just that logical knowledge of knowing you packed for four and then suddenly you need to provide for eight.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: On the bright side, we met a guy named Derek the other day who said he's with a group of people called the Responders.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: They seem to have realized what we knew all along... that the government wasn't going to lift a finger to help clean up this mess.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: The Responders have been at it from the start with no sign of order, so they took it upon themselves to organize and help those in need.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: It's also a relief to no longer be the only one with a real medical background and training.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: Derek said he can bring back some supplies and help out a bit. At least until we're more settled.

transcript.speaker: Ella
transcript.text: Lucy's been a great help, but her training as an aesthetician can only go so far.

items.name: Formation of the Brotherhood of Steel
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Hailey Takano
transcript.text: Appalachia online, Captain.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: I know most of you love America.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: The good old red, white, and blue.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: But those of us that served at Mariposa know something.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: America failed.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Not because its citizens, who lived clean lives filled with hardship in a never ending war.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: And certainly not because of its fighting men and women. God bless them.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: No, its leaders failed us. Senators, Generals, Presidents, all those bastards.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Their failure almost destroyed all mankind.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: But I look around here and I see survivors.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: People too stubborn, too damned ornery to die.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: We've fought and we've endured and finally we have a small patch of safety.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: But having a home isn't enough. We need something more.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: What we need is... purpose.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: But we cannot look to the America of old for that purpose.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: We have to build our own.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: So tonight, as we break bread together, let us forge together something new. Something strong.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Something we can be proud of. Something we can build upon.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: We'll preserve what's best of what's come before and use it. And one day, we will reclaim what was lost.

transcript.speaker: Roger Maxson
transcript.text: Let us forge a Brotherhood of Steel.

items.name: Jesus Sunday's Holotape - Part 1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: When my brother JD & I answered the call to head into Harpers Ferry, we expected to find an organized Free States stronghold.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Now that we're here, it's obvious that no one knows what the hell they're doing.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: The other Free States families are wasting precious resources trying to restore Harpers Ferry and create a safe haven for survivors.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Instead, they should be turning the town into a fort and stockpiling supplies to prep for the long haul.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: We'll still pitch in, but we don't plan on sticking around long to see what happens.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: We don't think that Harpers Ferry will ever be safe, so we're going to use our share of the supplies to reinforce the bunker at our cabin.

items.name: Jesus Sunday's Holotape - Part 2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: For the past few years, my brother's been bummed out - like really sad, you know?

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Personally, I don't think he's ever recovered from watching the world end. Hell, I don't think any of us have.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: I tried to talk to him about it, but he kept pushing me away and changing the subject.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: But after JD met Brianna Hawke in Harpers Ferry, things turned around. I guess she helped him out by giving him a different shoulder to cry on.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Why JD's more comfortable with her than his own brother, I'll never know.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Yeah, I'm kind of angry, maybe even a little jealous, but I'm going to let it go for his sake.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Still, there's something about Brianna that bugs me, so I'm going to keep an eye on her.

items.name: Jesus Sunday's Holotape - Part 3
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: We were at our bunker when the Scorchbeasts attacked Harpers Ferry. It took them less than an hour to burn the place down.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: When the attack was over, I thought Brianna was dead and that JD would return to his old self. When he didn't, I became suspicious.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Then Brianna shows up at our cabin with a small group of survivors and everything became clear.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: She had conned JD, played him this entire time, pretending to love him to give herself and her friends an invite to our bunker.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Well, there was no way I was going to let that happen. I told her she could march right back to her cave and find her own place to survive.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: When JD tried to stop me, I had to knock him out. That's when Brianna's people pushed back, and I fired some shots into the air to scare them away.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Now I have to deal with JD, and damn is he going to be pissed.

items.name: Jesus Sunday's Holotape - Part 4
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: It's been weeks since I chased off Brianna Hawke, and I feel like I've wasted all of it trying to convince JD that he was better off without her.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: I finally thought I was getting through, until I was cleaning up our cabin and found the goddamn notes they'd been passing to each other.

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: Instead of heading out to hunt, that hijo de perra's been stabbing me in the back by giving Brianna some of our supplies!

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: After everything I've sacrificed for our family, how could he do this to me?!

transcript.speaker: Jesus Sunday
transcript.text: When he gets back from today's "hunt" we're going to have a little chat about Brianna Hawke. And this time, I'm not going to just look the other way.

items.name: Message to Marge 1
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Marge. I keep recording these. Hoping one day I can make it home.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: I found these Brotherhood of Steel guys outside of Grafton.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Heard about them. Some weird military cult.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Seeing them in action... made me... I remember when my unit would roll in like that. All shock and awe.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: I'll tell you what, these Grafton raiders didn't stand a chance.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: One of them, Knight Moreno, noticed me. Came over and chatted.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Nice guy. Really made me rethink the stuff I've been told.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: It came out I was in the cavalry at Anchorage, he said they had a place for me.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Marge, I'm sorry. I've made it maybe 400 miles since the bombs.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: At this rate Texas might as well be a million miles further.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: I need... a unit. A place to belong. I feel like the Brotherhood may be it.

items.name: Message to Marge 2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Marge. It's been a couple weeks.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: I've had three squares, showers, working lights... Camp Venture's got power, proper power, Marge.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: I'd feel almost human if it weren't for the Senior Knight and the training.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: I graduated basic easy back in the day, and I know I may be a bit softer... but...

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Wilson's an Army Ranger, or well, was one. And the drills they're making us do.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: But as beat up and worn out as I feel, that first time getting back into the 51b.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: You can call yourself Knight, Paladin, Grand Poobah of the Roman Empire, I don't care.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Just don't take my power armor away.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: They're rushing training. A big battle with Super Mutants happening.

transcript.speaker: "Tex" Rogers
transcript.text: Good. I got some aggression I need to unleash.

items.name: Protecting Our Own
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Raleigh
transcript.text: I think it's time we claimed the Armory as our own territory.

transcript.speaker: Raleigh
transcript.text: I'll need to get Eddie and Niraj to help out with some security measures.

transcript.speaker: Raleigh
transcript.text: Survivors are gonna hate it, but we gotta protect our own, especially against the damn Brotherhood.

transcript.speaker: Raleigh
transcript.text: Derek told us they've been hitting up the Responders for manpower and supplies and not taking no for an answer.

transcript.speaker: Raleigh
transcript.text: Well, they've got another thing coming if they try that over here, and we need to be ready.

items.name: Restoring Order
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: Things are finally starting to shape up around here at Harpers Ferry.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: We got a lot of defenses up and running, a real perimeter, and people taking lookout shifts.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: Niraj is working on some new contraption to help with these brutal storms that sweep through. He said they could filter the air or something.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: And Ella's got a decent clinic set up with the help of the Responders.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: It makes me feel like maybe Raleigh was right, and we can have a real go at this.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: Some of these survivors proved they aren't completely worthless, too.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: One guy, Duncan, turned out to be a decent hunter, and another gal, Kendyll, she's a better shot than me.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: Still, you look at these people struggling here and just think... You bastards had your chance.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: We practically spelled it out for you and you just turned up your noses and called us crazy.

transcript.speaker: Eddie Hayes
transcript.text: Bunch of idiots...

items.name: Tossed the Stash
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: Hey Matt, I made it back to the safe house... but you probably guessed that.

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: Stupid, you're so stupid! He knows you made it to the safe house, you idiot! YOU IDIOT!

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: Umm... unfortunately, I had to stash the duffle on the way because I was being chased. I'm sorry, I'm really sorry, Matt.

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: Idiot! You stupid IDIOT!

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: So, yeah... I tossed it under the porch in the Southwest corner of the white hotel, the one up on the cliff.

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: Anyway... I'm gonna take off, Matt. It's too dangerous around here. I'm gonna head back into the mountains, I think. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: Chris Fatur
transcript.text: What the fu... farewell? Nobody says that. You're so stupid, you idiot. Stupid IDIOT!
